newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Benefun ends debut sharply higher.
newsitem.headline: Benefun ends debut sharply higher.

text.p: Investors rushing for a slice in China's growing retail market boosted Benefun International Holdings Ltd's shares to a sharply higher finish compared to their issue price on their first day of trading, analysts said.
Benefun's relatively low price to earnings (P/E) multiple, which created room on the upside, had made the stock particular attractive, they said.

The company's shares ended at HK$1.59, up HK$0.44 or 38.26 percent from their issue price of HK$1.15. The shares moved in a range of HK$1.46 to HK$1.82. Volume was 100.41 million shares worth HK$166.73 million.
"It performed very well today. Its China retail concept proved to be a success," said Ben Kwong, research director at Dharmala Securities.
Benefun, a unit of Singapore-listed Heshe Holdings Ltd, is engaged in retailing and manufacture of casual wear in China, Hong Kong and Taiwan.
"The stock was still cheap at the current price level compared with other retailers in China such as Glorious Sun," said Kinson Au, research manager at Asia Financial Securities.
Casual wear retailer Glorious Sun Enterprises Ltd trades at about 22 times P/E. Another retailer, Giordano International Ltd, trades at about 12 times.

Benefun issued 100 million new shares at HK$1.15 per share, giving a fully-diluted P/E of 7.9 times and a weighted average P/E of 6.5 times, in an initial public offer (IPO) in Hong Kong. Its Hong Kong IPO was 105 times oversubscribed.
"In the short run, profit-taking may cap its rise in view of the narrower gap between its P/E and others counterparts," Kwong said. "However, it is worth holding for longer term investment."

"The China retail sector is actually on a growth track," Au said. "The stock is expected to gain support from investors who want to tap the growing retail sector and the overall economic growth in China in the longer run."
